classification.difficultyReason: Transform branch conditions under −x, handle the zero boundary, compare with the original function and its negative, and confirm parity using restricted cubic and quadratic graphs rather than polynomial powers alone.

content.prompt: A polynomial with only odd powers is an odd function, and a polynomial with only even powers is an even function. These conclusions may not be valid for piecewise functions. Simplify each function at $-x$ and compare it with the original function and its negative to determine whether it is odd, even or neither. Graph each function to confirm your answer.

answer.short: Even: $f(-x)=f(x)$. Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\begin{cases}(-x)-(-x)^3,&-x<0,\\(-x)^3-(-x),&-x\ge0\end{cases}\\f(-x)&=\begin{cases}x^3-x,&x>0,\\x-x^3,&x\le0.\end{cases}\end{align*}$$At $x=0$, both cubic expressions equal $0$, so the boundary may be included in either branch. Thus $f(-x)=f(x)$ and $f$ is even. The graph has zeroes at $x=-1,0,1$ and passes through $(-2,6)$ and $(2,6)$.

spec.description: Symmetric cubic pieces with zeroes -1,0,1 and dashed guides to (+/-2,6).
spec.mathematics: y=x-x^3 for x<0 and y=x^3-x for x>=0.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}g(-x)&=\begin{cases}(-x)^2+1,&-x<0,\\(-x)^2-1,&-x\ge0\end{cases}\\g(-x)&=\begin{cases}x^2+1,&x>0,\\x^2-1,&x\le0.\end{cases}\end{align*}$$For example, $g(-1)=2$ and $g(1)=0$, so $g(-1)$ equals neither $g(1)$ nor $-g(1)$. Therefore $g$ is neither even nor odd. Draw the left half of $y=x^2+1$ with an open point at $(0,1)$, and the right half of $y=x^2-1$ with a filled point at $(0,-1)$.

spec.description: Left parabola ends at open (0,1); right parabola starts at filled (0,-1), crosses at (1,0), and has the source key-point guides.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2+1 for x<0; y=x^2-1 for x>=0.
